raw_response:
I would keep my farm mostly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest and most familiar way for me to make use of the land in Quzhou. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I would push it through with steady water, enough nitrogen for grain filling, and two pesticide sprays if disease or insects show up. After wheat harvest, I would put the same land straight into summer maize, because maize fits the local weather, uses the summer rain well, and gives me stable grain output. I would also keep a small piece in spring peanuts, not to chase something fancy, but to spread risk a little, bring in some cash, and avoid putting every mu into one grain line. I would not make the plan too complicated, because with my background and the way I work, I would rather do a few crops well than manage too many badly.
